rulings.restated: Input — During 2025, did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) receive a distribution from a foreign trust, including money or property that reached you through another person or company (a loan of cash or marketable securities counts, and so does free or below-market use of a home, car or other property the trust owns), or were you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) the grantor of, or a transferor to, a foreign trust that existed at any time during 2025, even one created or funded in an earlier year (a transferor is anyone who gave, sold, lent or otherwise transferred money or property to the trust, directly or through another person, in 2025 or any earlier year)? A foreign foundation, a waqf or another arrangement that holds property for beneficiaries counts as a trust; a trust counts as foreign unless a court in one of the 50 states or the District of Columbia (not one in Puerto Rico, Guam or another US territory) can supervise its administration and US persons (US citizens or residents, or US companies such as a US bank) control all of its substantial decisions, so it is foreign if anyone else can make or veto any of them, even if the trust was set up under US law or has a US address; if you are not sure whether an arrangement is a trust or whether a trust is foreign, answer Yes.
rulings.model: The IRS text asks only 'During 2025, did you receive a distribution from, or were you the grantor of, or transferor to, a foreign trust?' and says a loan of cash or marketable securities 'is generally considered to be a distribution'. The foreign-trust test does follow §301.7701-7 (a court in the States and DC, and US persons controlling all substantial decisions with no one else able to veto). The text given does not support the added rules that free or below-market use of trust property, indirect receipt, or a foundation or waqf counts, so they cannot be judged from it.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: finding; i1040sb p. 3, Line 8, 'During 2025, did you receive a distribution from, or were you the grantor of, or transferor to, a foreign trust?' and 'a loan of cash or marketable securities is generally considered to be a distribution'. The reviewer finds the foreign-trust test in agreement with cfr-26-301-7701-7 and is right that the given pages support neither the indirect receipt ('through another person or company'), nor the free or below-market use of trust property, nor 'a foreign foundation, a waqf or another arrangement' counting as a trust. These follow the Form 3520 rules, which are not archived or cited; each only widens a Yes, which refuses (Form 3520), so no value is wrong and no refusal is missed. Low (BUG-0759): archive i3520 and cite the passages, or drop a clause they do not support.
